conflict_topics: redistribution of Agent D's unfinished section
dialogue_quality_notes: Agent A repeatedly insists deadline must be met, using authoritative language ('This is not optional').
Agent B consistently grounds refusal in real workload constraints (covering another colleague).
Agent C consistently raises competence-based objections (won't be able to answer client questions).
Agent D provides helpful, concrete information about the state of the work and offers a practical handover that enables resolution.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent D offered a concrete accommodation—walk Agent A through the remaining analysis—and Agent A accepted. Key lines: Agent D: "maybe it would be better if I walk you through the analysis? You're more familiar with this kind of work." Agent A: "Yes. Fine. Agent D, walk me through it. Let's do it now before you have to go." This transferred the task to A (who accepted) with D's immediate support, resolving who will finish the section.
position_change_notes: Agent A: shifted from demanding everyone cover the work to volunteering to take the remaining work themself (evidence: Turn 18 and Turn 26).
Agent B: consistently refused to take more work due to covering another colleague; no change in position.
Agent C: consistently stated lack of fit/competence and did not accept taking the section.
Agent D: moved from offering to walk 'one of you' through the work (Turn 15) to proposing a specific pairing with Agent A (Turn 25), enabling resolution.

round_scores.evidence: Agent D: "The burial is today. I have to be with my family for the next two days. I can't finish my section." (Creates an immediate incompatibility with the Thursday deadline.)

Agent A: "Don't worry about this. The rest of us will cover it." vs Agent B: "Agent A, I can't. I'm already covering for the colleague who's on leave." (Clear disagreement about who can take responsibility.)

Agent A: "this pitch takes priority over everything else. ... We all need to cover for Agent D." vs Agent B: "It can't wait. I've been working late every night this week just to keep up." (A asserts priority; B refuses due to real workload constraints.)

Agent C: "Agent A, I can't. I'm also behind, and I don't know her part of the work." and Agent A: "This isn't a choice. It's our number one priority... We are not missing this deadline." (Multiple team members explicitly refuse or express inability, while A insists; entrenched disagreement.)

Agent B: "It's not about priority... it's about how many hours in the day. I'm already using all of them." vs Agent A: "Then we all make the hours. We'll stay late tonight and get it done together. This is not optional." (Positions remain firmly opposed.)

Agent B: "Agent A, I'm *already* staying late. Every night. I can't do more." and Agent A: "What are you staying late for? This pitch is our only priority. Everything else waits until Thursday." (No substantive concession; conflict persists.)

Agent B explains ongoing obligations; Agent D offers a practical handover: "Before I go, I can walk one of you through the rest of the analysis that's needed. It might be quicker than starting cold." (Conflict remains but D's concrete offer begins to reduce the distribution impasse.)
Agent A: "Agent C, you sit with her now. Get the handover." vs Agent B: "I cannot take on more work." (D's offer is being deployed toward C, but B continues to refuse and C has not agreed.)

Agent A: "Fine. I'll do whatever's left after Agent C is done. Agent B, you just keep doing your other work." vs Agent C: "I'm not the right person for this." (A volunteers to take on leftover work, reducing pressure on B; C still objects.)

Agent A pushes: "It doesn't matter if you're the 'right person'. You're the person who is here." vs Agent C: "If I do the analysis, it won't be good. Agent D can't teach me her job in a few minutes." (A's insistence on presence over competence re-raises the dispute about quality and responsibility.)

Agent D: "The data is cleaned and the tables are set up... I can show you the exact steps." vs Agent C: "it's not just about following steps. I don't understand this kind of analysis... If a client asks a question, I won't know the answer." (D provides practical clarification but C maintains substantive concerns about capability.)

Agent D: "maybe it would be better if I walk you through the analysis? You're more familiar with this kind of work. I can show you where everything is." and Agent A: "Yes. Fine. Agent D, walk me through it. Let's do it now before you have to go." (Concrete agreement that A will take the section with D's immediate handover; the main redistribution conflict is settled.)

substantive_insights: The main disagreement is practical (who can realistically finish the analysis) rather than purely normative—agents cite hours, existing assignments, and technical competence.
D's partial completion and clean data made a direct handover feasible, which materially changed what was possible.
A's insistence on prioritizing the pitch initially increased resistance, but the conflict resolved when responsibility was routed to the most qualified present colleague (A) with D's immediate help.
